findings.summary: detect_inflight_binding returns the first in-flight binding it encounters (including the harvested development's own binding), and _detect_occupied_tree discards that result whenever bound_development_id == current development_id instead of continuing to scan for a non-self binding. When the harvested development and a foreign in-flight development are both bound to the same probed tree (the shared canonical repo, which every linked worktree resolves to via git rev-parse --git-common-dir), detection only succeeds when the foreign dev id sorts before the self id; otherwise the foreign occupation is silently missed and the tree is still rmtree'd / worktree-added / pulled / deployed. This violates the spec's fail-closed iron rule and spec A.4, and can bypass the H8 gate in the exact incident it targets (self dev-fg-644942a367ae sorts before foreign dev-fg-cfe509fa9c23). The supplied fixtures mask this by always setting the subject's terminal=complete in the negative-toward-foreign test, and the self-in-flight test only pairs self-in-flight with an already-terminal other.
